correctness.rationale: An exact root inner product classifies squared distances 2,4,6,8. At squared 2 the maximal simplices are directed arcs sharing initial or terminal index; their good-cover nerve is K_{n,n} minus the diagonal matching, connected with n(n-1) edges and 2n nodes, yielding b1=n^2-3n+1 and the fixed-letter/two-cycle trace formulas via oriented cellular chains (root negation swaps and reverses bipartite edges). At squared 4, simplices are sets of arcs with disjoint source and target vertex sets. Their face-poset map to all nonempty disjoint (S,T) has lower fibers with maximum S×T; hence a homotopy equivalence to Hom(K2,Kn), whose disjoint probability-simplex pair (p,q) maps homeomorphically via p-q to boundary of the l1 ball in the sum-zero subspace. This proves sphere S^(n-2), with permutation/flip degree sgn(sigma)*(-1)^((n-1)epsilon). At squared 6 precisely the m=n(n-1)/2 reverse-root pairs are nonedges, so the complex is the join (S0)^*m=S^(m-1); the signed action on wedge^2 R^n has determinant sgn(sigma)^(n-1), root negation flips all m factors, giving (-1)^(m epsilon). At sqrt8 a full simplex forms. Degrees 1,n-2,m-1 are distinct for n>=5, so positive-degree persistent maps across distinct stages vanish; H0 merges at sqrt2. Independently calculated all pair-distance levels and adjacency conditions at n=4,5,6,7; n4 is a known already-published finite case, not a proof by extrapolation.
residual_risks: The equivariant lower-fiber comparison should be interpreted at the homotopy level; finite chain checks do not prove universal fixed-subgroup equivariance.
The degree-one module trace has an explicit chain argument; exact integral module presentation beyond sign characters was not asserted.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new complete ambient-Euclidean Rips filtration on type-A root configurations across every n>=5, not the already-known Hom(K2,Kn) sphere alone. Babson-Kozlov Proposition 4.3 gives the Hom sphere and its flip and is cited as a key ingredient. Ayzenberg et al study open/closed-hemisphere nerve complexes of type-A roots (acyclic directed graphs), which are NOT identical to pairwise Euclidean threshold cliques. Published finite n=4 cuboctahedron supplies only that special case and no all-n chars. Residual possibility of an unnamed all-rank Euclidean Rips statement remains.
residual_risks: General Hom(K2,Kn) topology and flip action are prior art; priority claimed only for exact Euclidean Rips identification, barcode and full S_n×C2 chars.
Only the analytic poset-fiber argument proves all n>=5; finite n=4..7 distance checks do not establish universal homotopy or group characters.

value.rationale: A closed all-rank type-A metric-topology computation for a natural root-system family is a useful structural classification. Connecting the Rips intermediate stage to Hom(K2,Kn) identifies a non-obvious sphere, while the exact graph nerve, crosspolytope stage, integral persistence and full natural symmetry traces give additional information absent from the known Hom sphere in isolation. The already-known finite cuboctahedron stage is not incorrectly claimed as new.
residual_risks: Intermediate Hom topology is known; mathematical value rests on all-rank filtration and symmetry, not on restating Babson-Kozlov.
